subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Should maintainers require fresh Windows/provider proof before closing this billing-context report, or accept the current source-level guardrails as sufficient?
rationale: The source guards look well placed, but the reported impact is provider billing and the exact current-main runtime path has not been proven after the latest session-history changes.

options.title: Require current-main proof
options.body: Keep this open until a packaged Windows or equivalent runtime run shows a fresh `--session` excludes trajectory sidecars from submitted context and provider input tokens stay proportional.

options.title: Close on source evidence
options.body: Accept the existing artifact, TUI, and reseed guards as sufficient and close without new runtime billing proof.

options.title: Add stronger guardrails
options.body: Ask for a narrow follow-up that blocks trajectory sidecars at the model-context boundary even if an unexpected path resolves them as session files.

recommendation.title: Require current-main proof
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a packaged Windows or equivalent runtime run shows a fresh `--session` excludes trajectory sidecars from submitted context and provider input tokens stay proportional.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision centers on TUI/session startup behavior plus recent current-main session-history changes, where Vincent Koc has the strongest recent history signal in this review.
